audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Shen, Shen, Skill, Skill, Mundo, Mundo, Mundo. Its own whys[] disagree on five of seven rows: whys[0] says you edge out level 1, whys[2] and whys[3] say Shen owns 3 through 5, whys[4] says his R tempo keeps him ahead at 6, whys[5] calls first item even.
audit.why: The packet chart is [Dr. Mundo, Shen, Shen, Shen, Shen, Skill, Dr. Mundo] and it matches the whys[] on every row except the last. Shen has no level-1 tools that beat Mundo's regen — Twilight Assault is 140 mana at rank 1 and Ki Barrier only exists after a cast — and from 2 onward his empowered autos and the block take over.
audit.corrected: L1 Dr. Mundo, L2-L6 Shen, first item Skill, 2+ items Dr. Mundo.

audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating and carryRating are empty strings, and level 6 was written as a Mundo spike.
audit.why: breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t both already say 'difficulty 6/10, Shen carry threat 6/10'. Level 6 is Shen's, not yours: Stand United is 200s at rank 1 but it is a map-wide play, and Maximum Dosage does not answer a Shen who is not standing next to you.
audit.corrected: diffRating 6/10, carryRating 6/10; phases[4] is Shen and its why now names Stand United's cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page states in five separate places that Spirit's Refuge blocks Infected Bonesaw. It does not. Also the brief's own missingInteractions entry claims Mundo's passive cancels Stand United's channel — that is false and I did not write it.
audit.why: Riot's text for Spirit's Refuge: 'Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked.' Attacks, not spells. Infected Bonesaw is a spell projectile at 975 range and passes through the zone; what dies inside it is your auto-attacks. This flips the entire trading pattern: you do not wait out the W, you stop autoing and keep throwing Q. Separately, Mundo's passive is a resist on himself, not an outgoing crowd-control effect — Mundo has no interrupt in his kit at all, so nothing he casts cancels Stand United. The real passive interaction is the other direction: Shadow Dash's taunt is an Immobilizing effect, so the first one is resisted and drops a cannister.
audit.corrected: whys[2], spikes[0].text, early, mid, wants.foe[0], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t now say the W blocks attacks and that Bonesaw goes through, and name the passive-versus-taunt interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: Only one cooldown appeared and no mana costs, despite mana being Shen's hardest early constraint.
audit.why: Shadow Dash is 18/16/14/12/10 for 150 mana; Twilight Assault is 8/7.25/6.5/5.75/5 for 140 at rank 1; Spirit's Refuge is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 for 40. A rank-1 Shen who dashes has spent most of his pool.
audit.corrected: Numbers now appear in breakdown.cooldowns, phases[0].why, phases[3].why and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading advice said 'don't dump abilities into an active W; wait it out'.
audit.why: Half of that is wrong for the same reason as point 4 — Q is not blocked, so waiting out the W concedes free poke. What you withhold inside the zone is autos.
audit.corrected: early and mid now say stop autoing, keep poking.

notes:
REJECTED A SUPPLIED INTERACTION. The brief's missingInteractions carries: "Shen's Stand United (R) is a channel — your Goes Where He Pleases (P) cancels it outright." That is false and I did not write it into any field. Mundo's passive is a resist applied to himself; it is not an outgoing crowd-control effect, and Mundo's kit contains no interrupt of any kind (Q slows, W and E deal damage, R heals). The rule almost certainly fired because the kit file tags Mundo's passive with a hardCC flag for parsing reasons. Worth fixing at the generator, because the same false pairing will fire on every channelled ultimate in the game.

The genuine large omission was the opposite of what the page said: Spirit's Refuge blocks ATTACKS, per Riot's own wording, so Infected Bonesaw passes through it and your autos do not. That claim appeared in five fields and I corrected all five.

Filled diffRating and carryRating, which were empty strings; values taken from breakdown.difficulty on the same page.

tradeGood, breakdown.trading and report[3].t still carry the generic template paragraph. I left them: the Shen-specific content went into early/mid where it has room, and rewriting the 386-character template inside the band three times over would have added no new fact.
